newsitem.title: CHINA: China sacks officials in Moslem region crackdown.
newsitem.headline: China sacks officials in Moslem region crackdown.

text.p: China has sacked 260 grassroots officials and cracked down on underground religious activities in a northwestern Moslem region where anti-Chinese riots last February left nine people dead, state media said.

The clampdown affected 35 Communist Party bosses of villages and towns in Yili district in Xinjiang region and 19 village mayors or factory managers, the Xinjiang Daily said in an edition seen in Beijing on Thursday.
Authorities launched a crackdown on underground religious activities in Yili, stopping the unauthorised construction or renovation of 133 mosques, the June 21 edition of the newspaper said.
About 40 core participants in illegal religious activities had been arrested, it said without giving further details.
"Illegal religious activities were cleaned up in Yili district village by village, hamlet by hamlet," it said.
"Yili district... has dealt a blow to key ethnic separatists, violent territorists and religious extremist leaders," the newspaper said.
Authorities broke up 105 illegal classes teaching the Koran and dispersed 499 students, it said.
The police force was increased by 459 officers and the militias in villages were increased by 266, the newspaper said.
Five pro-independence school officials were sacked, it said, adding that teachers would face dismissal for stirring up separatist sentiment.
Riots in Yili on February 5, which began as demonstrations for Xinjiang independence and then turned violent, left nine people dead and 198 injured.
Chinese authorities executed three rioters in April and police opened fire on a mob trying to rescue the death-row convicts, killing two people.
Turkish-speaking militants of the ethnic Uighur minority want to set up an independent East Turkestan in Xinjiang.
Xinjiang has been rocked by a string of bombings and other violent incidents since February.
In May, Chinese authorities executed eight people in the regional capital of Urumqi for bombings, murders and robberies.
The group planted home-made bombs on public buses that blew up within minutes of each other in Urumqi on February 25, killing nine people and injuring 58 others.
The attacks coincided with funeral rites in Beijing for paramount leader Deng Xiaoping who died in February aged 92.
Exiled separatists have vowed to stage more bombings until they gain freedom for their homeland.
The authorities seized 11 tonnes of explosives and uncovered 83 hideouts illegally selling firearms between March and May.
Xinjiang was shaken last year by bombings and assassination attempts on officials and Moslem leaders seen as loyal to Beijing.
Xinjiang borders Afghanistan, Pakistan and three mostly Moslem Central Asian states.
